digest.component_or_area: rebar-mcp HTTP transport and authentication layer
propositions: rebar-mcp today is stdio-only with no HTTP transport or per-request authentication; remote MCP clients cannot access it over the network.
The optional HTTP transport must support OAuth 2.1 Resource Server authentication, validating inbound bearer tokens and advertising RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata discovery.

A composite TokenVerifier acting as a single fail-closed choke point must re-validate every token's resource audience against the configured auth_resource_server_url to prevent token audience confusion and enforce resource binding.

Five pluggable token verifier modes (static bearer, JWKS/JWT, RFC 7662 introspection, trusted-proxy passthrough, custom) must be selectable via flat mcp.auth_strategies configuration and environment variables, with each populating AccessToken.resource.

HTTP transport with auth disabled must refuse to start unless REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP is set; unknown auth strategies, empty composite with auth enabled, and auth-enabled HTTP with no verifier must all fail-closed at startup.

DNS-rebinding and origin protection must be on by default with explicit loopback bind defaults; non-loopback bind requires host/origin allowlists and explicit TLS-at-edge acknowledgment to prevent bearer tokens crossing the network in cleartext.
